name: Can I start preconstruction before I own the lot?

mainEntity.name: Is it possible to do feasibility and early planning before closing on a property?
mainEntity.text: Is it possible to do feasibility and early planning before closing on a property?

acceptedAnswer.text: It is often possible to begin early feasibility and preconstruction planning before you own the lot, especially if you want to understand whether the property can support your goals. This stage may include zoning review, public records research, preliminary budgeting, and a high-level assessment of site constraints. In some cases, you may also be able to do limited site investigations if the seller allows it. This approach can be very helpful when buying a property in Los Angeles, where lot conditions, setbacks, slope, and neighborhood requirements can strongly affect what is possible. Early analysis can tell you whether the lot is likely to support the home you want or whether the project will require compromise. The main limitation is access and authorization. Without ownership or seller approval, some site work may not be possible. Even so, a qualified design-build team can still provide useful early guidance based on available records and assumptions. If you are considering a purchase, ask for a feasibility-first scope rather than full design. That lets you make a smarter acquisition decision before committing to the lot. It is far better to discover a constraint early than after you have already closed and started design.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes. Buyers often start feasibility and preconstruction planning before closing, especially when they want to confirm zoning, buildable area, likely costs, and site risks. Early planning can help you decide whether the property supports your goals. The scope should be limited until ownership, access, and permission to investigate the site are confirmed.
